note: Facts only a human may decide. An agent must never guess a value here. UNRESOLVED renders as a visible placeholder in the published pages and makes `pnpm portal:publishable` fail, which is what the deploy step runs. The repository gate only checks that the published pages match these sources, so the tree stays green while these are pending.

operator.businessRegistrationNumberRationale: Individual developer publishing without a Korean business registration. Null is a decision, not a missing value.

contact.supportEmailVerifiedNote: Flip to true only after a message sent to this address from outside the account has been confirmed received. It is published on the privacy policy, the deletion page and the Play listing, and it is the only channel a user who cannot open the app has.

audience.childDirectedRationale: Not child-directed; minimum age 14. Derived from repository evidence and cited law, not from preference. (1) Content is general-knowledge study material -- English vocabulary, Korean proverbs, four-character idioms, world landmarks -- not preschool material. (2) The app ships no ad SDK and no telemetry SDK (tests/contracts/data-safety-claims.test.ts fails if one is added without updating the Data safety declaration), so the Families ad restrictions are not what drives the answer. (3) 개인정보 보호법 제22조의2 requires 법정대리인 동의 before processing a under-14 personal data, and this codebase has no guardian-consent flow anywhere -- sign-up is Google/Kakao OAuth or email+password with no age gate. Declaring under-14 would make the app non-compliant on the day it ships. 14 is the statutory threshold, and it also satisfies Play target-audience declaration. RISK TO REVIEW: the pet-collection art is deliberately cute, and Play assesses declared audience against imagery and terminology, so the store assessment may still push toward a mixed-audience classification. If that happens the answer changes and a neutral age screen becomes required.

retention.rationale: deletionReceiptMetadata is not a choice: RECEIPT_TTL_DAYS = 30 in apps/server/src/privacy/account-deletion-store.ts is passed to request_account_deletion_v1 as the receipt TTL, so 30일 is what the system already does. accountDataAfterDeletionRequest is a published ceiling rather than a measured constant -- the migrations encode no grace period and no scheduled delay, access blocks on receipt and the worker advances one stage per tick, so disposal is far faster than 30 days and the promise is one the code can keep. backupPurgeWindow stays UNRESOLVED because it is bound to the production Supabase backup and PITR configuration, and no cloud project exists yet. See docs/release-evidence-blockers.md.

urls.originRationale: The Vercel deployment origin. Play needs a public privacy-policy URL and a public account-deletion URL on this host, and the Android App Link in the release manifest is pinned to it.

processors.name: Supabase
processors.regionRationale: The production project does not exist yet, so its region is undecided. Cross-border transfer disclosure depends on it.

processors.name: Google LLC
processors.regionRationale: Only when the user chooses Google sign-in.

appLinks.fingerprintsRationale: Play App Signing owns the release certificate, so these cannot be known until the app exists in Play Console and a bundle has been uploaded. While the list is empty the generator emits no .well-known/assetlinks.json — an assetlinks file with no fingerprints does not fail open, it fails verification and is worse than no file. The OAuth callback stays on the touchcatch:// custom scheme until then.
